title: Florida Panthers sign goaltender Louis Domingue to one-year contract - Central Broward News
text:
The Florida Panthers have signed goaltender Louis Domingue to a one-year, two-way contract for the remainder of the 2025-26 season. The announcement was made by Bill Zito, President of Hockey Operations and General Manager of the team.
Domingue, who is 33 years old, has played seven games this season with the Charlotte Checkers in the American Hockey League (AHL), recording a 3-3-0 record. He also appeared in 11 games for Novosibirsk Sibir in the Kontinental Hockey League.
Throughout his career, Domingue has played in 144 NHL games for several teams: New York Rangers (2023-24 to 2024-25), Pittsburgh Penguins (2021-22), Calgary Flames (2020-21), New Jersey Devils (2019-20), Tampa Bay Lightning (2017-18 to 2018-19), and Arizona Coyotes (2014-15 to 2017-18). His NHL statistics include a record of 61 wins, 60 losses, and 10 overtime losses, with a .906 save percentage and a goals against average of 3.01. He has also participated in seven NHL playoff games with the Lightning and Penguins.
In addition to his NHL experience, Domingue has played in 233 AHL games across multiple teams including Charlotte, Hartford Wolf Pack, Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins, Stockton Heat, Binghamton Devils, Syracuse Crunch, Springfield Falcons, and Portland Pirates. His AHL record stands at 104 wins, 92 losses, and 23 overtime losses with a .905 save percentage and a goals against average of 2.82.
Before joining the professional leagues, Domingue spent four seasons in the QMJHL playing for Moncton Wildcats and Quebec Remparts. In the 2011-12 season he led the league with a .914 save percentage.
Domingue was selected by the Phoenix Coyotes as the 138th overall pick in the fifth round of the 2010 NHL Draft.
The Panthers are coming off consecutive Stanley Cup championships in both 2024 and 2025. Single game tickets remain available through SeatGeek.com or FloridaPanthers.com/tickets.
